## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Treatment
where: TreatmentService (uses), src/business/treatmentService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
return this.treatments.create({ hiveId, productId, startDate, endDate });
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B

=====SOURCE-END=====

response.rationale: A Treatment is one application to a hive. It is created as `this.treatments.create({ hiveId, productId, startDate, endDate })` in src/business/treatmentService.ts. A Treatment Product is the catalogue item applied, stored separately in TreatmentProductRepository (`private readonly items = new Map<string, TreatmentProduct>();` in src/persistence/repositories.ts). The treatment points to the product through productId, so this is a reference between two concepts, not one concept under two names. The graph agrees: TreatmentService calls TreatmentRepository.create and TreatmentProductRepository.create as separate methods.
